name: Mijamin
overview: Mijamin was a male Aaronic priest from the tribe of Levi, mentioned in the book of Nehemiah. He is listed among the signatories of the sealed covenant document in Nehemiah 10:1-27, specifically noted in Nehemiah 10:7. His priestly role highlights his service in the restoration period following the return from exile.
namesAndTitles: The name Mijamin means 'from the right hand' in Hebrew, as recorded in Nehemiah 10:7. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaning that may imply strength or favor.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Mijamin was a descendant of Aaron, linking him to the priestly lineage established by God. Beyond this inferred relationship, no additional family connections are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mijamin's significance lies in his role as an Aaronic priest who participated in the covenant renewal under Nehemiah's leadership. His inclusion among the sealed signatories demonstrates his commitment to uphold the laws and reforms essential for the spiritual restoration of Israel. This reflects the ongoing importance of the Levitical priesthood in maintaining covenant faithfulness during the post-exilic period.
